tagline: The first K-pop Worlds anthem, built on Deft's unbreakable heart.
headline: NewJeans became the first K-pop group to sing a Worlds anthem, soundtracking Deft's underdog story and Faker's fourth title.
summary: Released on October 4, 2023 (KST), GODS made NewJeans the first K-pop group to sing a League of Legends Worlds anthem, and its animated video retold Kim "Deft" Hyuk-kyu's road from Mapo High School to the 2022 world title. Fans were split on the song, but the video had the biggest first day of any Worlds anthem, and NewJeans' live debut of it opened a final in which Faker's T1, the video's final bosses, won a fourth world title. Three years on, its roughly 157 million views are the most for any Worlds anthem video released after 2019.

story.heading: The first K-pop voice of Worlds
story.body:
In 2023 Worlds returned to South Korea for the first time in five years, with the final booked for Seoul's Gocheok Sky Dome. For the tenth anthem in the series, Riot turned to NewJeans, whose EP *Get Up* had debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 that summer. LoL Esports announced *GODS* on September 26, 2023, and Rolling Stone and Korea JoongAng Daily both noted that NewJeans were the first K-pop group to provide a Worlds anthem.

The writers were familiar names. Riot Games principal composer Sebastien Najand and Alex Seaver of Mako wrote and produced the song, Serban Ghenea mixed it, and the video was made with the animation studio PSYOP. For NewJeans it was a sharp turn away from their usual pop and R&B sound: they sang entirely in English over heavy synths and a choir. The group called it a new experience and said it had been fun to try a new genre and sound. At Worlds media day Danielle admitted they had first doubted they could do justice to the song's energy, and Haerin later told Billboard they chose English lyrics so fans around the world could connect with the song more easily.

story.heading: An unbreakable heart
story.body:
The video's YouTube description calls it the story of "an unbreakable spirit and the unbending heart of a champion." To Korean fans, that wording pointed straight at one phrase. In October 2022, right after DRX lost its first Worlds group-stage game to Rogue, Kukinews reporter Moon Dae-chan interviewed Deft in New York. Deft said the team could still win as long as it did not fall apart from within, and Moon summed that up in his headline as *"the important thing is an unbreakable heart"* (중요한 건 꺾이지 않는 마음). DRX went on to win the whole tournament from the play-in stage, and after the title Deft quoted the line himself on social media.

By December the phrase had spread far beyond esports. A fan's handmade Korean flag bearing it was waved during South Korea's last-gasp World Cup win over Portugal in Qatar, and Son Heung-min repeated it in an interview after the team got home. *GODS* builds the phrase into the anthem: a sign on the wall of Deft's high-school classroom in the video quotes his "unbreakable" line, and the song's bridge ends on the words "heart, unbreakable."

story.heading: Deft's decade in four minutes
story.body:
According to LoL Esports, the video follows Deft from discovering League in high school to the 2022 run in which DRX "overcame all odds". Dot Esports' scene-by-scene breakdown fills in the details. It opens on a snowy morning at Mapo High School, where Deft sits at the back of a classroom while his schoolmate Faker is in the foreground. At home, Deft is still fighting a blue buff when Faker's Zed takes Baron Nashor, a nod to Faker's first world title in 2013.

The years of near-misses follow, each one staged in a different landscape. In a desert, Samsung Blue's 2014 run ends against Samsung White's PawN on Jayce. In a forest, Fnatic's Rekkles on Kennen ambushes Deft and Meiko, echoing Fnatic's 2015 sweep of EDG. On the ice in 2020, Keria raises Braum's shield against DAMWON's ShowMaker on Syndra, at what turned out to be Deft and Keria's last Worlds as teammates. Deft then crashes through the ice and sinks into dark water. During the bridge he kneels in a shaft of light until Zeka, Pyosik, BeryL and Kingen pull him to his feet. From there DRX cuts through the 2022 bracket: his old support Meiko on Renata Glasc, Gen.G's Doran on Renekton and, at the summit, T1's Keria and Faker. A Bard portal brings the whole team to Deft's side, Caitlyn's ultimate ends the fight, and the Summoner's Cup goes up.

The last scene looks ahead to 2023. Hopefuls from every region, including FURIA's Ayu, G2's Hans Sama, Cloud9's Blaber, JDG's 369, Gen.G's Chovy, GAM's Levi and PSG Talon's Azhi, look up at the trophy Deft has just won.

story.heading: Premiere night, and a split verdict
story.body:
*GODS* premiered on the League of Legends YouTube channel at 2 p.m. KST on October 4, 2023, and Riot invited Deft to watch it go live. The marketing-analytics firm Zoomph counted 67,903 people waiting before the premiere began and a peak of 116,791 watching at once. The video drew 7.8 million views in its first 24 hours, which Korea JoongAng Daily reported as the most-watched first day for any Worlds anthem. It reached No. 1 on YouTube's trending list in Korea, charted in 46 regions and passed 17 million views within a week. The song peaked at No. 41 on Spotify's global chart and entered the Billboard Global 200 at No. 75.

Fans were divided. Many Reddit users praised the storyline but called the song middle-of-the-road, said it did not sound like NewJeans, or wanted a bigger, more dramatic chorus. The most common comparison was *RISE*, the 2018 anthem built around Ambition's similar title run, which several fans felt was more epic.

story.heading: GODS on the Rift
story.body:
During the tournament the title picked up a second meaning. Team BDS top laner Adam was known for four bruisers, Garen, Olaf, Darius and Sett, whose initials spell GODS. BDS came back from 0–2 down to beat PSG Talon 3–2 in the qualifier for the main event, a series that Esports Charts measured at 1.3 million peak viewers. Afterwards ONE Esports ran an exclusive interview with him under the headline "'GODS' set for a makeover", because he was eyeing Tryndamere as a new main.

The anthem's main character had a harder year. Deft had moved to Dplus KIA, which went out in the Swiss stage with a 2–3 record, and Meiko's EDward Gaming did not qualify at all.

story.heading: Live at Gocheok Sky Dome
story.body:
On November 19, 2023, NewJeans performed *GODS* live for the first time in the finals opening ceremony at Gocheok Sky Dome. The same weekend they also made their Billboard Music Awards performance debut, and Danielle later called the pairing surreal. Minji told Billboard it was the stage with the most diverse range of creative elements they had done so far. Dancers and actors shared the stage with augmented-reality effects: a colossal Mordekaiser appeared over the audience, an actor carried Leona's shield, and the set ended with Leona defeating Mordekaiser. Danielle and Hanni said the group's outfits were based on Leona, with accessories made to resemble her golden armor. The song ended with NewJeans around the Summoner's Cup as the two finalists, Weibo Gaming and T1, were revealed on stage. The same ceremony hosted the first live performance of HEARTSTEEL's debut song *PARANOIA*.

The group had met both teams backstage at media day, and Hyein said she was glad to tell the players from both sides that they would be cheering for them. One of those players had a personal connection. Keria, Deft's old support and one of the video's final bosses, is a self-proclaimed NewJeans fan whose comments about the group had often gone viral, and before the semifinals he said he badly wanted to see NewJeans at the final. Faker, for his part, said he had listened to *GODS* a lot and found it grand. The official clip of the performance has since passed 20 million views.

story.heading: Once you play GOD
story.body:
Later that day T1, the team the video had cast as Deft's last obstacle, swept Weibo Gaming 3–0 in front of a sold-out crowd of 18,000. It was T1's fourth world title, the most by any team. It was also Faker's fourth, after 2013, 2015 and 2016, which made him the only player to win four. Zeus was named Finals MVP, and Keria, who had lost to Deft in the 2022 final, finally lifted the cup. The final peaked at 6.4 million concurrent viewers, not counting Chinese platforms, which was then the all-time record for a single esports event.

In hindsight, the chorus fit the winners almost as well as the hero. T1 had reached the title by knocking out three LPL teams in a row, LNG, JD Gaming and Weibo, and the song's rivals who "crumble one by one" read like a summary of that run.

story.heading: Legacy: the anthem that outlived its doubts
story.body:
Three years on, *GODS* has about 157 million views on the League of Legends channel. That puts it fifth among Worlds anthem videos, behind *Warriors*, *RISE*, *Legends Never Die* and *Phoenix*, and ahead of every anthem released since, about 30 million clear of the next one, 2025's *Sacrifice*. On Spotify the track has passed 278 million plays. Critics have warmed to it as well. ONE Esports (2024) and Esports Insider (2025) both rank it fifth among all Worlds anthems, and ONE Esports called a female group taking centre stage a historic moment for LoL Esports.

*GODS* also brought three big Korean stories of 2022–23 together in one season: one of K-pop's fastest-rising groups, a phrase that had travelled from an esports interview to the World Cup, and the T1 title that made Faker a four-time world champion. Like *RISE* five years earlier, it made the previous year's champion the hero of the next year's anthem. The difference this time was that the video's final bosses went on to win the tournament the song was written for.

whyItMatters: NewJeans became the first K-pop group to sing a Worlds anthem, the tenth in the series, in the year Worlds returned to South Korea.
The video is a full biography of Deft, from Mapo High School to the 2022 title, with real rivals (PawN, Rekkles, ShowMaker, Meiko, Doran, Keria, Faker) for fans to decode scene by scene.
It built Korea's "unbreakable heart" phrase into Riot's official anthem. The phrase came from a Kukinews interview with Deft at Worlds 2022 and was later carried to the World Cup on a fan's flag.
It had the most-watched first day of any Worlds anthem video (7.8M views in 24 hours) and entered the Billboard Global 200.
NewJeans' live debut of the song opened a record-setting final, in which T1's Faker and Keria, the video's final bosses, won the world title.
At about 157M views it is the most-watched Worlds anthem video released after 2019, and it has passed 278M plays on Spotify.

communityMoments.title: NewJeans revealed as the Worlds 2023 voice
communityMoments.description: LoL Esports announced GODS, sung by NewJeans and written by Sebastien Najand and Alex Seaver of Mako, with a video built around Deft's story.

communityMoments.title: Deft watches his own story premiere
communityMoments.description: Riot invited Deft to watch the premiere. About 67,900 people were waiting before it began, and viewing peaked at 116,791 concurrent viewers.

communityMoments.title: Biggest first day for a Worlds anthem
communityMoments.description: The video drew 7.8 million views in 24 hours, reached No. 1 on YouTube's trending list in Korea and charted in 46 regions.

communityMoments.title: Decoding the Easter eggs
communityMoments.description: Fans and outlets went through the video frame by frame and found Mapo High School, Faker's 2013 Zed, PawN's Jayce, Rekkles' Kennen, an alpaca plushie in Deft's bedroom and a classroom sign quoting his unbreakable-spirit line.

communityMoments.title: Onto the Billboard Global 200
communityMoments.description: GODS debuted on the Billboard Global 200 at No. 75, about two weeks after release.

communityMoments.title: Garen, Olaf, Darius, Sett
communityMoments.description: Team BDS top laner Adam's four signature champions spell GODS. After his reverse sweep of PSG Talon, ONE Esports ran with the pun in its headline.

communityMoments.title: Faker: "I've listened to GODS a lot"
communityMoments.description: After T1's semifinal win, Faker said his teammates' talk had introduced him to NewJeans and that GODS sounded grand. Keria said he wanted to see NewJeans at the final and win the title.

communityMoments.title: NewJeans meet the finalists
communityMoments.description: At Worlds media day the group said Deft's story in the video had resonated with them, and they reacted happily to Keria, a self-proclaimed NewJeans fan whose comments about them often went viral.

communityMoments.title: The live premiere at Gocheok Sky Dome
communityMoments.description: NewJeans performed GODS for the first time in the finals opening ceremony, with dancers, an actor carrying Leona's shield and an augmented-reality Mordekaiser looming over the crowd.

communityMoments.title: The final bosses win
communityMoments.description: T1 swept Weibo Gaming 3–0 for Faker's fourth world title, with Keria, Deft's old support and the video's other final boss, alongside him.

communityMoments.title: Ranked among the all-time greats
communityMoments.description: Two years later, Esports Insider ranked GODS fifth of all Worlds anthems, ahead of every other anthem from the 2020s except Heavy Is The Crown.

keyMoments.label: Winter at Mapo High
keyMoments.description: Deft trudges through a snowy alley to school, the start of a story that LoL Esports said begins with him discovering League as a high-school student.

keyMoments.label: The classroom
keyMoments.description: Deft sits alone at the back of the classroom, beneath a wall sign that Dot Esports reads as his unbreakable-spirit line; Faker appears in the foreground.

keyMoments.label: Faker's Zed takes Baron
keyMoments.description: Still fighting a stone sentinel, Deft looks on as Faker's Zed leaps in and carves up Baron Nashor, a nod to Faker's 2013 world title.

keyMoments.label: First chorus
keyMoments.description: Faker's Zed leaps across a giant moon as the first "Once you play GOD" chorus begins, and Deft looks up at him.

keyMoments.label: The hook drops: first Worlds stage
keyMoments.description: As the GA-GA-GODS hook arrives, Deft sits on a floodlit Worlds stage, then lands in a desert duel with Samsung White's PawN on Jayce (2014).

keyMoments.label: Rekkles in the forest (2015)
keyMoments.description: Now with EDG, Deft and Meiko are ambushed in a dark forest by Fnatic's Rekkles, whose Kennen lightning tears through them.

keyMoments.label: Keria's shield (2020)
keyMoments.description: On the ice, Keria raises Braum's shield against ShowMaker's Syndra orbs, at Deft and Keria's last Worlds as teammates.

keyMoments.label: Sinking
keyMoments.description: The ice shatters under Syndra's blast and Deft drifts down into dark water as the music falls away.

keyMoments.label: Bridge: on his knees
keyMoments.description: On "I'm on my knees", Deft kneels alone in a shaft of light and reaches upward.

keyMoments.label: DRX lifts him up
keyMoments.description: A hand grabs his and the 2022 DRX roster, Zeka, Pyosik, BeryL and Kingen, pulls Deft back to his feet as the bridge asks who will read this underdog story.

keyMoments.label: Meiko, then Draven
keyMoments.description: Meiko appears with Renata Glasc's staff, the final chorus kicks in and Deft's Draven axes cut him down, the 2022 quarterfinal against EDG. YouTube marks this stretch as the video's most replayed.

keyMoments.label: Doran's Renekton
keyMoments.description: Next up is Gen.G's Doran, another former teammate, swinging Renekton's blade before Deft answers with Varus.

keyMoments.label: The final bosses: Keria and Faker
keyMoments.description: Deft trades blows with Keria's Karma, then Faker's Viktor knocks him flat and the two T1 players stand over him, recreating the 2022 final.

keyMoments.label: Bard's portal
keyMoments.description: A golden Bard portal opens and the whole DRX team appears beside Deft above the clouds as the GODS hook returns.

keyMoments.label: Caitlyn's ultimate
keyMoments.description: Deft lines up Caitlyn's rifle for the final shot, and the sky above the clouds erupts.

keyMoments.label: Lifting the Summoner's Cup
keyMoments.description: Back on the stage, Deft raises his fists, embraces his teammates, and DRX lift the trophy through falling confetti.

keyMoments.label: The next challengers
keyMoments.description: The cup is reflected in an eye, and then the 2023 hopefuls, including FURIA's Ayu, Gen.G's Chovy, GAM's Levi and PSG Talon's Azhi, stand before it.

keyMoments.label: NewJeans take the Worlds stage
keyMoments.description: All five members open the Worlds 2023 finals ceremony with the first-ever live performance of GODS.

keyMoments.label: Mordekaiser rises
keyMoments.description: The arena turns green as an augmented-reality Mordekaiser looms among the dancers.

keyMoments.label: Leona strikes
keyMoments.description: An actor carrying Leona's shield raises her sword toward an eclipsed sun, and a giant golden blade sweeps across the arena.

keyMoments.label: The finalists
keyMoments.description: Weibo Gaming and then T1 are revealed on stage, before NewJeans finish the song around the Summoner's Cup.

featuredClip.description: Bard's golden portal flares open on a cloud-top plateau and Deft's 2022 DRX teammates appear beside him, weapons in hand, as the GA-GA-GODS hook returns and they charge at Faker and Keria.
